<div class="vc_tta-container" data-vc-action="collapse"><div class="vc_general vc_tta vc_tta-tabs vc_tta-color-grey vc_tta-style-classic vc_tta-shape-rounded vc_tta-spacing-1 vc_tta-tabs-position-top vc_tta-controls-align-left"><div class="vc_tta-tabs-container"><ul class="vc_tta-tabs-list"><li class="vc_tta-tab vc_active" data-vc-tab><a href="#tab1" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Cash / Forward</span></a></li><li class="vc_tta-tab" data-vc-tab><a href="#tab2" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Fixed Basis</span></a></li><li class="vc_tta-tab" data-vc-tab><a href="#tab3" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Price Later</span></a></li><li class="vc_tta-tab" data-vc-tab><a href="#tab4" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Deferred Payments</span></a></li><li class="vc_tta-tab" data-vc-tab><a href="#tab5" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Firm Offers</span></a></li><li class="vc_tta-tab" data-vc-tab><a href="#1669136101049-d3f62263-e2e5" data-vc-tabs data-vc-container=".vc_tta"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Fixed Futures Contract</span></a></li></ul></div><div class="vc_tta-panels-container"><div class="vc_tta-panels"><div class="vc_tta-panel vc_active tabbed" id="tab1" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#tab1" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Cash / Forward</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element " >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>A cash or forward contract allows you to establish the delivery month, quantity, and price for your corn.</p>
<p><strong>Features</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Guarantees a cash price</li>
<li>Potential to capture market carry</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Advantages</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Simplest type of contract</li>
<li>Can take advantage of favorable current market for future delivery months</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Disadvantages and Risks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Cannot take advantage of further improvements in futures/basis</li>
<li>Corn must be of sufficient quality to be purchased by Christensen Farms</li>
</ul>
<p style="padding-left: 30px;"><strong>Example:</strong> On March 4th, you establish a $3.44 cash price for corn you’ll be delivering in October.</p>

		</div>
	</div>
</div></div><div class="vc_tta-panel" id="tab2" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#tab2" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Fixed Basis</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element " >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>A fixed basis contract allows you to lock in a basis when you believe it is more favorable now than it will be later. You now have the ability to lock in a futures price within a specified time period before delivery.</p>
<p><strong>Features</strong></p>
<div class="list arrow">
<ul>
<li>Guarantees a local basis price</li>
<li>Establishing a price level can be delayed until a later time</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Advantages</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Timely delivery of corn based on contracts and storage</li>
<li>Provides flexibility to participate in markets and determine a cash price when you want</li>
<li>No storage fees</li>
</ul>
<div class="divider"><strong>Disadvantages and Risks</strong></div>
<ul>
<li>Only protects a small portion of price risk. Futures risk is greater than basis risk</li>
<li>You bear the risk of any changes in the price levels over the life of the contract</li>
<li>Requires you to pay attention to the futures markets and determine best time to establish a cash price</li>
<li>Corn must be of sufficient quality to be purchased by Christensen Farms</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong>Example: </strong>On February 3rd, you lock in a basis of -$.33 to the July board on 10,000 bushels to be delivered in June. The current CBOT futures price for July is $3.97. The cash price on February 3rd would therefore have been $3.64. On May 10th, you decide to establish your futures for your contract. July board is now $4.07 and your cash price is $3.74.</p>

		</div>
	</div>
</div></div><div class="vc_tta-panel" id="tab3" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#tab3" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Price Later</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element  ]" >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>A price later contract allows you to deliver corn now, have flexibility to participate in markets, and lock in a price at a later date.</p>
<p><strong>Features</strong></p>
<div class="list arrow">
<ul>
<li>Deliver corn without establishing any price</li>
<li>Must be priced by the date specified in the grain policy at the time of delivery</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Advantages</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Deliver corn immediately and eliminate storage risk</li>
<li>Take advantage of basis/futures improvement</li>
<li>Can price the entire contract at once or in small quantities.</li>
</ul>
<div class="divider"><strong>Disadvantages and Risks</strong></div>
<ul>
<li>Downside price risk is unlimited</li>
<li>Payment isn’t made until contract is priced</li>
<li>Ownership transfers to buyer</li>
<li>Handling or storage fees may apply</li>
<li>Corn must be of sufficient quality to be purchased by Christensen Farms</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong>Example: </strong>On November 8th, you deliver corn on price later. The current cash price is $3.80. On April 14th you decide to price your contract at current cash price, $4.50, less any incurred fees.</p>

		</div>
	</div>
</div></div><div class="vc_tta-panel" id="tab4" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#tab4" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Deferred Payments</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element " >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>A deferred payment contract allows you to delay payment for your corn.</p>
<p><strong>Features</strong></p>
<div class="list arrow">
<ul>
<li>Delays payment for corn deliveries</li>
<li>Cash, Forward, Fixed Basis, and Price Later contracts can be deferred</li>
</ul>
<div class="divider"><strong>Advantages</strong></div>
<ul>
<li>Payment cannot be made until deferred date in contract</li>
<li>Deferred Payment Contracts need to be established prior to settlement</li>
</ul>
<div class="divider"><strong>Disadvantages and Risks</strong></div>
<ul>
<li>Downside price risk is unlimited</li>
<li>Payment isn’t made until contract is priced</li>
<li>Ownership transfers to buyer</li>
<li>Handling or storage fees may apply</li>
<li>Corn must be of sufficient quality to be purchased by Christensen Farms</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong>Example: </strong>On October 20th, you deliver and sell 12,000 bushels and set up a deferred payment to be made on January 1st of the upcoming year, or any date of your choice.</p>

		</div>
	</div>
</div></div><div class="vc_tta-panel" id="tab5" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#tab5" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Firm Offers</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element " >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>Capture market opportunities by placing a firm offer with us. You determine the bushels, your price target and delivery month, and offer duration (day, week, and month). When the market hits your price target, your contract goal will be achieved. We will notify you and provide you a written contract.</p>

		</div>
	</div>
</div></div><div class="vc_tta-panel" id="1669136101049-d3f62263-e2e5" data-vc-content=".vc_tta-panel-body"><div class="vc_tta-panel-heading"><h4 class="vc_tta-panel-title"><a href="#1669136101049-d3f62263-e2e5" data-vc-accordion data-vc-container=".vc_tta-container"><span class="vc_tta-title-text">Fixed Futures Contract</span></a></h4></div><div class="vc_tta-panel-body">
	<div class="wpb_text_column wpb_content_element " >
		<div class="wpb_wrapper">
			<p>Fixed Futures contracts permit you to set a futures price level and leave the basis open.  Farmers who enter fixed futures contracts typically like the current price level but believe the basis will strengthen.</p>
<p><strong>Features</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Locks in your futures price</li>
<li>Allows you to capture market carry</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Advantages</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Protected against falling futures price levels</li>
<li>Basis could strengthen</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Disadvantages and Risks </strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Cannot benefit from higher futures prices</li>
<li>Basis could weaken</li>
<li>Must be done in 5,000 bu. increments</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Example: </strong>Assume on June 1, a producer agrees to sell 5,000 bushels of corn on a fixed futures contract.  At the time, December futures are at $6 and the current basis for October delivery is -.45.  On September 1, the basis strengthens to -.35 so the farmer decides to set the basis for October delivery, resulting in a cash sale price of $5.65 per bushel ($6 Futures Price-$.35 basis).</p>

		</div>
	</div>
